observation.visible_scene: A close, static shot of a crushing setup: a large cylindrical metal press head occupies the top center, a yellow-and-black diagonally striped cylindrical base sits at the bottom, and between them is a stack of white ceramic bowls decorated with a peach-like fruit and red Chinese characters. At the first frame the upper bowls are already broken into a jumble of curved white shards, while the lowest decorated bowl remains mostly whole beneath the pile. A pale beige wall with two recessed vertical panels forms the background.
visible_changes: The metal press head moves downward only slightly and very gradually across the clip, narrowing the gap to the shard pile.

The pile of broken shards shifts, compresses, and ejects fragments sideways and downward; a curved white piece on the right detaches and tumbles outward, and fine dust/debris streaks appear on the left side.
A crack line becomes visible and persists on the right side of the lower decorated bowl, and small chips break off its rim over time.
The lower decorated bowl stays centered and largely intact in form, though its visible surface pattern and position relative to the base remain essentially fixed.
Background and camera framing do not change, indicating object motion rather than camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the initial shattering of the upper bowls and the prior motion of the press head before this segment.
Whether the lower bowl ultimately collapses or survives after the clip ends.
The exact mechanism/identity of the press and the material of the bowls beyond visual appearance.
uncertain_details: The descent of the press head is small; it may be a slow continuous motion or quasi-static loading—only a slight positional change is supported.
Some flying pieces are motion-blurred, so their precise trajectories are uncertain.
Whether dust streaks are airborne debris or motion blur of fragments is not fully distinguishable.
